dimensions.assessment: Affects Medicare Part D plan sponsors, Medicare Advantage plans, pharmacy benefit managers, commercial health plans, and millions of plan enrollees.
dimensions.evidence: each contract entered into with a PDP sponsor under this part... shall provide that such sponsor may only enter into a contract with a pharmacy benefit manager...

dimensions.assessment: Imposes strict bidding rules, net effective cost guarantees, audits, civil monetary penalties, restitution requirements, and star rating performance measures.
dimensions.evidence: shall be subject to a civil monetary penalty of not more than $100,000 per violation.

dimensions.assessment: Imposes significant regulatory and compliance costs on plans and PBMs, potential civil penalties, and introduces oversight structures aimed at controlling prescription drug costs.
dimensions.evidence: aggregate savings attributable to the bidding process required under subsection (i)

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Social Security Act and ERISA across multiple sections, introducing standardized PBM bidding, mandatory audits, risk-based monitoring, and quality rating adjustments.
dimensions.evidence: To amend title XVIII of the Social Security Act, and the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, to create certain requirements with respect to pharmacy benefit managers.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent ongoing regulatory, auditing, and reporting requirements taking effect primarily for plan years starting on or after January 1, 2028.

missing_information: Precise federal administrative costs to execute the required audits and data collection.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill creates extensive new standardized bidding, transparency, auditing, and oversight requirements for pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) within Medicare Part D, Medicare Advantage (MA-PD), and commercial health plans governed by ERISA.
